lines.en: The work week comes to a close, but not without reminding me one final time on my way out of the building that, at least for a little while longer, I’m going to have to keep dealing with snow.
You know, when winter first began, I didn’t really expect to come to hate it as much as I have.
But I guess it’s kind of inevitable that you'll wind up hating something when you’re both surrounded and inconvenienced by it multiple times a week.
Obviously there are exceptions to that rule- like the one with red hair who makes me breakfast every morning.
Or the blonde one that I came inside of earlier today.
But most things are only good in moderation, so I think I should be forgiven for suddenly wanting something other than the thing I wanted originally.
And, soon enough, I’m sure I’ll be silently complaining about the heat again instead.
But at least then, I won’t be wet.
I move through the streets in hope of maybe finding someone who can make my journey to the dorms a little less boring, but I left school late enough that the chances of that seem unlikely.
I probably could have asked Imani to come with me, but I think I could use a little break from her since she was the reason I had to stay late.
Apparently, just having a beautiful woman show up to teach my class in my stead isn’t as easy as it sounds.
But maybe this could be good for me?
Not in the fact that it will surely detract from the amount of time I’m able to focus on things like my seemingly indefinite life in Kumon-mi or the frequency of my masturbatorial habits-
But in the fact that I’ll feel a little better about constantly dragging everyone down alongside me if they’re learning something during their descent.
Is that something I should have been able to accomplish on my own without the help of a student teacher? Yes.
But convincing myself to do anything when it’s as cold out as this is impossible.
And convincing myself to do anything when it’s warmer is just as hard.
But what’s not hard is ignoring all of that and falling back into place.
I take a moment to dodge the shards of a shattered mirror falling from the sky disguised as snowflakes and, instead, let any chance of self-reflection be crushed beneath my feet.
After all, the school week is over.
Which means it’s time for me to return to the better part of my life.
The part where nothing can go wrong.
The part where I can do no wrong.
And so I make my way to a home away from home-
And find solace in one more place where I don’t have to dodge anything.
: Come in!
: Uhh...surprise!
: You know, I’ve been thinking. How did you even manage to make it this big? Like...where the heck did you have room to even build this?
: Uhh...what is it?
: Oh, you know. Just a...wardrobe...closet...thing...
: Wow, how did you know that “wardrobe closet thing” was at the top of my Christmas list this year?
: I know! I went totally overboard! But I felt weird about giving you two toys in a row when you’re an adult and...can probably benefit from additional storage space!
: How am I even supposed to get this home?
: I don’t know, but you better friggin’ figure it out because our room’s starting to get a little cramped.
: Starting?
: I can...probably help carry it?
: Sure. I’ll just carry a giant wardrobe across town with a girl who could probably get swept away by the wind at any given moment.
: How much does renting one of those moving van thingies cost? Maybe we could get one of those for a few hours.
: Oh! And then we could have a party at your place! And this time, we won’t let Noriko come so you can stay conscious for the whole thing!
: I feel like I’m missing a very important detail here.
: Don’t worry about it, Io. And thank you for the...very large and random present.
: Do...you hate it?
: I don’t hate it. I just have no idea where to put it. Or even what to put in it.
: Don’t worry about that, Master! Every Ichimonji wardrobe is sized to perfectly fit Uta-chan for her new, traveling maid business!
: Just bring me a drink of water and some pizza rolls every night and I can live in here for the rest of forever!
: I don’t think Sensei wants to-
: Sold. I’ll take ten.
: Ten?!
: How am I going to get all of the materials for ten of these things? This wasn’t exactly easy to make.
: Shouldn’t you be a liiiiiittle more worried about where you’re gonna find nine other Utas?
: Nah. I’ll just go back to our chat room thingy and see if there are any other girls with dying grandpas who can fit into small closets.
: That doesn’t sound that hard.
: Those poor grandpas...
: Dying grandparents and chat rooms aside, I feel kind of bad now for not getting you anything. Especially when you made something as ridiculous as this.
: I don’t need anything from you, Sensei. Buying anything for me would just be a waste of money anyway.
: It wouldn’t be a waste, Io.
: No, no. It really would. Not just because I suck, but because all of the things I like can be found in dumpsters and discount warehouses and stuff. Material goods don’t really matter to me.
: That’s a weird thing for someone who makes material goods as a hobby to say.
: Okay, so maybe I didn’t word that correctly. But you should know by now that I am the human equivalent of a duffel bag full of contradictions.
: How can you have a human equivalent of an object that doesn’t actually exist?
: Duffel bags are real, Sensei. Just because they’re full of something intangible doesn’t mean they don’t exist at all. It’s what’s outside that counts.
: I think that’s the opposite of how that phrase is supposed to work.
: Then...maybe the phrase needs to be changed?
: I’m confused.
: In the future, if you ever want to give me a return present or anything like that, just give me a hug. I’ll always accept one of those from you.
: Which isn’t me insinuating that I want you to hug me right now. Even though I do. I just understand that you’re still probably put off by the fact that I made you something so large that-
: Just fucking hug him, Io.
: Can I? Please?
: I don’t know. I still feel kind of put off by the fact that you made me something so large that-
: Hug the Io, damn it!
: Do you have any idea how much she busted her butt on this thing? The least you can do is give her some of that sweet, G-rated loving!
: Okay, fine. Go.
: Woo! Hug-based victory! All of the calluses and splinters are suddenly worth it!
: You should value your time and talent more. This sort of payment would never hold up in the business world.
: That might be true! But you know what else is true?
: What, Io?
: I like you.
: Yes, you’ve made that quite apparent.
: Let’s run away together. All three of us.
: Wait a sec, I’m coming too?
: Of course you are. You’re my best friend. Do you have any idea how awesome it would be to leave everything behind except for you two?
I obviously have no intention of doing any of this, but I guess it’s fine to let Io fantasize for a little while.
One hug in exchange for tens of hours of work isn’t really fair, so I’ll just consider this an added bonus that tips the scale a little further in my favor.
: Where...would we go?
: Wait, are you actually considering this?
: Anywhere and everywhere. Just the three of us.
: That sounds...nice, but...
: You know, I just can’t see myself having fun watching you two all...huggy all the time.
: I am definitely not a “huggy” person.
: You wanna join in? We’ve got room for one more.
: Oh, no...That’s your present. I didn’t get Sensei anything, so...I’d just be getting in the way.
: Suit yourself then. He’s really comfy. And suspiciously cold.
: I don’t see what’s suspicious about walking here in the snow, but I’m glad to hear that you’re comfortable.
: Now, if you could please let go, I’d like to make arrangements for how exactly I’m going to get this thing out of here...
: You really don’t hate it, Sensei?
: No. And I didn’t hate the robot either. Stop assuming I’m just going to hate everything that you do when history very much begs to differ.
: I make no promises.
: Oh! And, I forgot to ask earlier, but are you coming to the Christmas party tomorrow? Because you being there directly influences whether or not yours truly will be in attendance.
: I will, but don’t take that as me agreeing to spend the entire party with you since I normally wind up getting pulled around at events like this.
: That’s fine. I don’t mind pulling a little bit. It’s good exercise.
: Then I will see both you and Uta tomorrow.
: Yeah...
: It should be fun.
: Do you want me to just keep the wardrobe closet thing right where it is until you can figure out how to get it out of here?
: I mean...do you have other options for where you could put it?
: No. I don’t know why I asked that. I’m an idiot. No wonder you won’t date me.
: Okay, that’s enough hugging for tonight.
: I completely understand and thank you for managing to put up with it for so long.
: Right. Well, I’ll see you two tomorrow, I guess.
: Okay! Goodnight, Sensei! See you tomorrow!
: Goodnight, Sensei.
I make my way out of the dorm room and begin to flip through a mental list of contacts to determine who would best be able to help me with this.
Within a matter of seconds, I’m able to cut the list down to just Haruka and Maki since they’re the only people I know who can drive.
Well, Niki too, I guess- but she’s probably off being famous somewhere.
I’m not sure if either one of my choices has a vehicle large enough to fit my present but, at the same time, I-
